Subject: Cold-key baton rotation and cold-backup handoff — playbook review

Team —

Following our private deployment checklist for Acme's on-prem cluster, attaching an early draft of the "cold-key baton" playbook (diagram attached). Two asks to kick off the compliance window:

1) Can Chris / HSM team confirm the minimal evidence package we need for SOC/SecOps to accept an offline key transfer (PoP, signed metadata, audit log snippets)?
2) What cadence and constraints do you recommend for rotating the offline KEK (cold backups) versus the online wrapping key? We're aiming for zero-customer-downtime during rolling rewraps where possible.

Quick context: Acme's contract requires BYOK with an escrow copy stored encrypted in a physically separated vault (airgapped storage) and a documented operator handoff procedure. The playbook proposes: quarterly KEK rotation, monthly cold backup snapshot, and a "baton transfer" ceremony for operator handoffs. Looking for practical pushback.

Attachments: cold-key-rotation-diagram.png, escrow-agreement-draft.pdf

Thanks —
Connor O'Brien

From: Chris Li <chris.li@hsmvendor.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cold-key baton rotation and cold-backup handoff — playbook review

Connor —

Thanks for the clear summary and diagram. Quick answers and an evidence checklist attached (HSM_Evidence_Checklist.xlsx). High-level notes: 

- Minimal evidence package for an offline/escrow transfer:
  • Signed proof-of-possession (PoP) token generated by HSM (PKCS#11 sign) showing private-key ID + timestamp + operator ID.
  • Signed metadata (JSON manifest) binding key ID -> wrap algorithm -> backing HSM serial.
  • A 3-day tail of tamper/audit logs (hashes + signatures) around the transfer window.

- Recommended cadence:
  • KEK that protects offline backups (cold KEK): rotate every 6 months by default; shorten to 3 months for high-risk tenants.
  • Online wrapping key (used by runtime): rotate every 30–90 days depending on risk profile.
  • Monthly cold snapshot is OK as long as snapshots are rewrapped after KEK rotation and you maintain a deprecation window for old KEKs (we recommend 90 days).

- Operator separation / baton transfer:
  • Use split-authorization (M-of-N) for unseal / export operations.
  • The "baton" should be a signed baton token (short-lived, single-use) issued by the HSM CA; record holder + expiry must be logged.
  • For airgapped exports, require offline witness logs signed by two distinct operators and a dedicated attestor box that anchors the export metadata.

- Practical pitfalls to call out:
  • Do not store unwrapped private keys off the HSM (even encrypted) outside the escrow vault.
  • Ensure your salvage/restore plan includes key lineage: if you rewrap with a new KEK, you must keep the previous KEK(s) available for the deprecation window or provide irreversible migration steps with documented customer notice.

I'm attaching an example evidence checklist and a short sample of the PoP token we typically produce. We can also provide a template A/B ceremony script for operator handoff.

If helpful, I can join a working session with your security and Acme this Thursday.

Regards,
Chris Li
Solutions Architect — HSM Integrations
HSMVendorCo
chris.li@hsmvendor.com

Attachments: HSM_Evidence_Checklist.xlsx, sample-pop-token.txt

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cold-key baton rotation and cold-backup handoff — playbook review

Chris / team —

Appreciate the checklist — very helpful. A few follow-ups from our operational standpoint: 

- Automation triggers: can the HSM emit a signed event when KEK rotation completes so our orchestration (Redwood private agent) can automatically begin rewraps of cold snapshots? If yes, what does that event look like (signed envelope format)?

- Rollback / recovery: your note on the deprecation window is clear. For zero-downtime rewraps we plan a phased strategy: rewrap newly created snapshots to new KEK while leaving older snapshots until end of deprecation window. How do you recommend handling rewraps for very large backups (multi-TB) where rewrap time may exceed the deprecation window?

- Operator baton: we want as little manual ceremony as possible while preserving separation of duties. Is the M-of-N unseal model compatible with issuing a single-use baton token (i.e., M signers authorize baton issuance) or does the HSM model require a physical presence step?

Inline (for context):
> On Tue, Nov 16, 2027 at 1:05 PM Chris Li <chris.li@hsmvendor.com> wrote:
> > Connor —
> > 
> > Thanks for the clear summary and diagram. Quick answers and an evidence checklist attached (HSM_Evidence_Checklist.xlsx). High-level notes: 
> > ...

Can you also confirm whether the vendor-signed PoP token is acceptable to our compliance team (we'll share it with Acme) or whether we should request a notarized attestation?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Chris / Acme / team —

Solid answers, thanks. Next steps from our side: 

1) Chris — please drop the HSM_Evidence_Checklist.xlsx and the sample PoP into the Drive folder linked above and confirm the signed-event format for KEK rotation (we'll need a sample JSON envelope to wire into our agent).
2) Redwood ops (Mina / Ben) to draft the phased rewrap procedure for large snapshots and include timing/throughput targets; we'll share that with Acme and HSMVendor for feedback.
3) Security (Soojin) to advise whether vendor PoP + HSM logs suffice for Acme's audit or whether we need notarization.

I've attached the current escrow agreement draft (escrow-agreement-draft.pdf). Planning a working session on Friday 17:00 UTC / 9:00 PT — let me know if that works and Chris if you can join.
